lines.text: Tom had one small piece of bread left in the whole world.
And he was about to give half of it to a cat.
He ground wheat into flour at the old mill by the river.
Tom's oldest brother got the mill.
His middle brother got the donkey.
"I can't buy dinner with a cat!"
lines.speaker: Tom

lines.text: He looked at his last piece of bread.
Then he broke it in half, and gave one half to the cat.
The cat was sleek and orange, with white paws and bright green eyes.
He ate slowly, every last crumb.
Give me a bag and a pair of boots, and I will make you rich."
lines.speaker: Puss

lines.text: "A cat in boots looks important," said the cat.
lines.speaker: Puss

lines.text: Tom did not know what to think.
But he had nothing else, so he found an old bag and a tiny pair of boots.
He walked down the road like he owned it.
"From now on, call me Puss," said the cat.
lines.speaker: Puss

lines.text: The next morning, Puss had a plan.
He took his bag to the edge of the forest and filled it with fresh red berries.
Then he marched up the hill to the castle.
The king sat on his throne.
He had a long white beard and a tiny gold crown.
"The Marquis of Carabas sends you a gift."
lines.speaker: Puss

lines.text: "The Marquis of Carabas?" said the king.
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: (A Marquis is an important lord, and Puss thought it sounded fancy.)
He wanted the king to remember it.
The next week, Puss brought sweet peaches and warm bread.
"From the Marquis of Carabas," he said.
lines.speaker: Puss

lines.text: "Never heard of him," said the king, with his mouth full.
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: The week after that, Puss brought a jar of golden honey.
"Never heard of him," said the king, licking his sticky fingers.
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: I really must meet this Marquis."
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: Then, one morning, Puss was walking through the village when the town crier rang his bell.
"The king and the princess will ride past the river today!"
lines.speaker: Crier

lines.text: This was the chance he was waiting for.
He ran home as fast as his boots could go.
Tom sat in the cold river, shivering.
Puss hid Tom's old clothes under a rock.
Then he ran to the road and waved his paws.
"The Marquis of Carabas?" said the king.
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: A servant ran to the river with the clothes.
Tom hid behind a bush and put on a blue jacket, new pants, and shiny shoes.
When he came out, the princess smiled.
"Please, ride with us," said the king.
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: Puss waited until nobody was looking, then slipped away through the trees.
Now Tom looked like a Marquis.
But a Marquis needs land and a castle.
And Puss knew just the place.
Puss ran ahead of the carriage.
The fields, sheep, and apple trees along this road belonged to a mean ogre, and everybody was tired of him.
Puss still had a basket of peaches.
He traded it for warm cookies at the village bakery.
Then he gave one cookie each to the farmers, the shepherd, and the apple picker.
"Say these belong to the Marquis of Carabas," he whispered.
lines.speaker: Puss

lines.text: "Help me, and I will do my best to chase the ogre away."
lines.speaker: Puss

lines.text: "Whose fields are these?" asked the king.
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: "These fields belong to the Marquis of Carabas!" said the farmers.
lines.speaker: Farmers

lines.text: "These sheep belong to the Marquis of Carabas!" said the shepherd.
lines.speaker: Shepherd

lines.text: "Even the sheep agree," said the king.
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: "These apples belong to the... um..." said the apple picker.
lines.speaker: Picker

lines.text: A boot poked out from behind a tree.
"Marquis, you are so rich!" said the king.
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: Puss ran ahead again, all the way to the end of the road.
He had made a big promise.
Now he had to keep it.
There stood a huge castle with tall stone towers and colorful flags.
A big doormat said BEWARE OF OGRE.
The ogre who lived there was twice as tall as the door, with a voice like thunder and fluffy pink slippers.
(Nobody had the courage to tell him they were pink.)
Puss walked up to the door.
It played a happy little tune: Ding-a-ling-a-ling!
"I hear you can turn into any animal.
lines.speaker: Puss

lines.text: The ogre turned into a lion.
(Puss pretended he meant to do that.)
The ogre turned back into himself, and Puss climbed down.
The ogre was a tiny mouse.
The mouse zoomed out the door and down the hill, leaving one fluffy slipper behind.
Now it needed a new owner.
He hurried to the gate just as the royal carriage rolled up.
"Welcome to the castle of the Marquis of Carabas!" said Puss.
lines.speaker: Puss

lines.text: Tom stepped out of the carriage and looked at the huge castle.
The king trusted him, and it was all lies.
"Your Majesty," said Tom, "I must tell you the truth.
lines.speaker: Tom

lines.text: Puss covered his eyes with his paws.
"A real Marquis does not say 'um,'" he said.
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: "And I still have never heard of the Marquis of Carabas.
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: But I like an honest young man, Tom.
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: Would you like to marry my daughter?"
lines.speaker: King

lines.text: That night, after all the happy news, Tom and Puss ate supper in the castle kitchen.
There was one warm loaf of bread.
Tom broke it in half, and gave one half to Puss.
So Tom lived in the castle with the princess.
He had the softest bed in the castle, and wore his favorite boots everywhere.
All because of one small piece of bread, shared with a hungry cat.
Remember: a little kindness can come back to you in a big way.
